fr.elements: Main Residence; Circular Driveway; Access Drive; Landscaped Area; Open Terrain; Detached Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the access drive so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with tall reflective posts on both sides to keep it visible at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Post a clearly visible property map or layout sign near the driveway entrance showing the location of the main residence and detached structure.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can travel the full length without obstruction.
• Keep the circular driveway clear of parked vehicles so arriving fire or medical units can pull forward and turn around without maneuvering around obstacles.
• Designate and mark a specific staging area within the circular driveway where a second arriving unit can park without blocking the primary access route.
• Keep the turnaround path of the circular driveway free of planters, decorative boulders, or landscaping features that reduce the usable turning radius for large vehicles.
• Cut back vegetation growing against or directly adjacent to the detached structure to create clear space around all sides.
• Thin dense vegetation along the access drive at intervals to reduce the risk of fire spreading along the route responders must use to reach the property.
• Keep a gate or barrier at the single access point unlocked or equipped with a Knox Box so responders are not delayed gaining entry.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Grass Cover; Open Terrain; Scattered Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation; Open Green Space
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim or remove shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin the tree cluster near the structure to create open space between individual trees and between the trees and the house.
• Remove low-hanging branches on trees close to the house so flames cannot climb from shrubs into the tree canopy.
• Scatter or spread out the shrubs surrounding the structure so there is open ground between individual plants and the house.
• Cut and remove dry or dead grass close to the house, especially where it connects ground cover to nearby shrubs or trees.
• Keep the full length of the driveway clear of overhanging branches so fire trucks and emergency vehicles can reach the house without obstruction.
• Mow or cut grass along both sides of the driveway to reduce the chance of fire burning directly up to the road surface.
• Move any wood piles, stored materials, or other burnable items away from the house and outbuildings.
• Thin scattered trees across the property so open ground separates them rather than allowing branches to overlap and connect.
• Clear shrubs and tall grass immediately around any detached structures or outbuildings on the property.
• Maintain visible open ground between the green space areas and the house so there is a clear, unburned gap around the structure.
